cross_references.notes: DRC MoH May 21 bulletin (670 suspected, 61 confirmed, 160 deaths) confirmed by Reuters/CNBC Africa and France 24; earlier CDC page (575 suspected, 51 confirmed, 148 deaths) represents an earlier May 21 cut; both are internally consistent with rapid escalation trajectory; South Kivu case confirmed by AFC/M23 rebel authority and corroborated by UN spokesman and multiple wire services but not yet by DRC MoH or WHO; no scholarly publications indexed yet.

locations.name: Mongbwalu Health Zone
locations.notes: Suspected index health zone and epicentre; high-traffic gold-mining area where WHO received first alert on 5 May 2026; initial super-spreader event linked to a burial or health facility; INRB samples from this area confirmed BDBV on 15 May.

locations.name: Rwampara Health Zone
locations.notes: One of the primary hotspots; 8 of 13 INRB samples from this zone tested positive on 15 May confirming BDBV; on 21 May residents protested after relatives disputed Ebola as cause of a young man's death, with police firing warning shots.

locations.name: Bunia Health Zone
locations.notes: Provincial capital and major healthcare hub; early HCW cluster identified here in early May; field hospitals being established as of 18 May after Bunia General Referral Hospital became overwhelmed; confirmed cases reported.

locations.name: Nyakunde Health Zone
locations.notes: Cases identified on 18 May 2026; site of Nyankunde Hospital where American physician Peter Stafford contracted BDBV while treating patients.

locations.name: Goma
locations.notes: One confirmed case reported 17 May — a woman who travelled from Ituri; city of over 1 million under M23/AFC rebel control with airport closed since January 2025; one confirmed case under strict medical supervision as of 21 May per M23 authorities.

locations.name: Butembo
locations.notes: Cases identified 18 May 2026; epicentre of the devastating 2018–2020 Ebola-Zaire outbreak, raising fears of recurrence; deep institutional trauma and population treatment avoidance documented from that prior episode.

locations.name: Bukavu (rural area near provincial capital)
locations.notes: First confirmed case in South Kivu reported 21 May by AFC/M23 rebel alliance; 28-year-old male who travelled from Kisangani (Tshopo Province) — hundreds of km from Ituri epicentre — died and was buried safely; a second case under investigation; UN also confirmed a separate South Kivu case (a woman contact of two individuals from Beni).

locations.name: Kampala
locations.notes: Two lab-confirmed imported cases with no apparent link to each other, confirmed 15–16 May; first case was a 59-year-old Congolese male admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital 11 May, died 14 May; second confirmed 16 May in a traveller from DRC; no local transmission confirmed as of 20 May per WHO.

locations.name: Fort Portal
locations.notes: A group of Ugandans attended a burial in eastern DRC around 18 May, returned to Uganda, and some developed Ebola-compatible symptoms; symptomatic individuals taken to Fort Portal for treatment and isolation; under active investigation.

timeline.event: Estimated date of first suspected death in the outbreak per WHO experts; virus believed to have circulated undetected for approximately 2 months before formal confirmation.
Index case — a nurse — presents with fever, hemorrhage, vomiting and malaise at a medical centre in Bunia, Ituri Province, DRC; later dies. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH)

Suspected index case — a nurse at Evangelical Medical Centre, Bunia — develops fever, bleeding, and severe weakness; dies within days. Retrospective investigation suggests she was infected by a patient, implying community transmission was already ongoing.
Earliest known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia — reports symptom onset (fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting); dies at Bunia medical centre. (WHO DON602)
Index case: healthcare worker in Bunia develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and intense malaise — first known suspected case of the outbreak, later dies at a Bunia medical centre.

Suspected index case — a healthcare worker in Bunia, Ituri Province — develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and intense malaise; the individual subsequently dies. This is the earliest known suspected case.

First known suspected case: a healthcare worker in Bunia HZ develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and intense malaise; the individual subsequently dies. First confirmed index of symptomatic disease.
First known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia, Ituri Province — develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and malaise; later dies at a medical centre in Bunia. (WHO DON602)
Earliest known suspected case: health worker in Bunia, Ituri Province, develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and malaise; dies ~27 April.

First confirmed death: a health worker in Bunia, Ituri Province, develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting and malaise; body repatriated to Mongbwalu mining zone for burial, triggering super-spreader funeral event.
Earliest known suspected case: health worker in Bunia, Ituri, develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and malaise; later dies at a medical centre in Bunia (WHO DON602).
Second case reported in Ituri; samples sent to Kinshasa — test methodology defaults to Zaire ebolavirus Xpert assay, returning false-negative results; outbreak continues undetected.
Cluster of unexplained haemorrhagic fever deaths flagged in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, DRC.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown etiology in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths of four health workers within four days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including deaths among healthcare workers; initial GeneXpert tests in Bunia return negative for Zaire Ebola.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality cluster of unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 health-worker deaths within 4 days.
WHO alerted to unknown illness with high mortality in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including four healthcare worker deaths within four days.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri Province, including deaths among four healthcare workers within four days.
WHO alerted to unknown illness with high mortality in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri, including four health worker deaths within four days.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone including 4 health-worker deaths; rapid response team dispatched to Ituri.
WHO alerted to unknown high-mortality illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri, including reports of 4 healthcare workers dead within 4 days; rapid response team dispatched.

WHO alerted to high-mortality outbreak of unknown illness including HCW deaths in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri; initial Xpert tests negative for Ebola-Zaire — 10-day diagnostic delay begins due to BDBV-specific genomic divergence (~30%) from Zaire ebolavirus.
MSF receives alerts of increased hemorrhagic fever deaths in Mongbwalu; team deployed finds 55 deaths since early April. (MSF statement)
59-year-old Congolese man admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, Uganda with severe symptoms; later confirmed as first imported BVD case in Uganda. (Africa CDC / Uganda MoH)
Elderly Congolese man admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, Uganda, with severe Ebola-compatible symptoms (later confirmed BDBV-positive on 15 May).
Rapid-response teams investigate Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 13 blood samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa for advanced analysis. (WHO DON602)
WHO rapid-response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones. (WHO DON602)
WHO/DRC rapid-response teams conduct in-depth field investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara Health Zones; samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa.
WHO rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones; 13 blood samples from Rwampara sent to INRB Kinshasa for analysis.
WHO/DRC rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones; samples sent to INRB Kinshasa. (WHO DON602)
Rapid response teams complete in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZ; initial Xpert Ebola tests on 20 samples return negative because assay targets Zaire ebolavirus only.
WHO rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 20 samples collected, initially test negative using standard Ebola Xpert (Zaire-only assay).
INRB Kinshasa analyses samples; PCR confirms Orthoebolavirus in 8 of 13 specimens; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). (WHO DON602 / INRB)
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 confirmed Orthoebolavirus-positive by PCR on 15 May. Second Uganda imported case confirmed in Kampala on 16 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara; 8 test positive by PCR for Orthoebolavirus. (WHO DON602)
INRB analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; results released 15 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples; standard Xpert tests in Bunia earlier returned false negatives for all 20 samples tested, as the test detects only Zaire ebolavirus.
INRB Kinshasa receives 13 blood samples from Rwampara HZ for analysis; initial field Xpert tests had been negative for Zaire ebolavirus, causing a ~3-week diagnostic delay.
Initial Xpert tests on 20 Rwampara samples at Bunia Provincial Public Health Lab return false-negative for Ebola virus; samples forwarded to INRB. (WHO DON602)
First Kampala case dies. INRB analyses 13 samples from Rwampara HZ.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR. Genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) on 15 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara HZ; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR on 15 May; genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV).
Bundibugyo virus confirmed by laboratory (8 of 13 samples positive). First confirmed case detected in Kampala, Uganda.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms imported BVD case — 59-year-old Congolese male who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, on 2026-05-14. (DRC MoH / Uganda MoH / Africa CDC)
Africa CDC activates Incident Management Support Team; convenes urgent cross-border coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, WHO and partners. (Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; INRB confirms 8 positive samples by PCR, genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case — a 59-year-old Congolese man who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala.

INRB genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call. (WHO DON602; Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC; genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV/Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense). Uganda MoH simultaneously declares outbreak following first confirmed imported case in Kampala (Kibuli Muslim Hospital). Africa CDC convenes urgent high-level regional coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan and 130+ global partners.

INRB confirms 8 of 13 samples positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination statement: ~246 suspected cases, 65 deaths.

INRB confirms Bundibugyo virus in 8 of 13 samples. DRC MoH officially declares DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported BVD case (59-year-old Congolese male who died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC alerts continent and convenes emergency regional coordination meeting with 130+ participants.

INRB confirms Bundibugyo virus (Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) by PCR in 8 of 13 samples; DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Kampala death). Africa CDC issues continental alert. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH / Africa CDC)

INRB confirms Bundibugyo virus in 8 of 13 samples by PCR; genomic sequencing confirms BDBV species. DRC MoH declares 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case. Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak; 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths across Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia. Uganda MoH concurrently confirms first imported BVD case (59-yr-old Congolese male, died 14 May, Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala).
Africa CDC issues continental alert; CDC issues Level 3 Travel Health Notice for DRC and Level 1 for Uganda; 65 contacts listed in DRC, 15 classified high-risk.
DRC Ministry of Health officially declares the country's 17th Ebola outbreak (2nd BDBV) in Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia HZs. Uganda MoH simultaneously confirms imported BDBV case in Kampala.

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC. Uganda MoH confirms first imported BDBV case (Kampala). INRB confirms BDBV in 8/13 samples from Rwampara HZ. Africa CDC issues continental alert. CDC issues Level 3 (DRC) and Level 1 (Uganda) travel health notices.
Second confirmed Kampala case (fatal). Suspected Kinshasa case reported (later retracted).
Second imported confirmed case identified in Kampala with no apparent link to the first; suspected Kinshasa case tests negative on confirmatory INRB PCR and is disconfirmed. (WHO PHEIC / INRB)
WHO Director-General determines the Bundibugyo outbreak in DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC); does not meet pandemic emergency criteria. (WHO)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Uganda; determination cites 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri plus 2 confirmed cases in Kampala and 4 HCW deaths. Africa CDC holds 130-participant high-level consultative meeting.

Second imported case confirmed in Kampala (unlinked to first). WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC. 246 suspected cases, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri confirmed at this time-point. (WHO PHEIC declaration)

Second unrelated confirmed case reported in Kampala, Uganda. WHO Director-General declares a PHEIC under IHR Article 12 — without convening an Emergency Committee, citing the gravity of the situation. Africa CDC activates its Incident Management Support Team.

WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC (declared without Emergency Committee, a first in WHO history). Second imported case confirmed in Kampala. Kinshasa alert issued; later retracted after confirmatory INRB testing negative.

WHO Director-General Tedros declares PHEIC without convening an Emergency Committee — a historic first. Second unlinked imported case confirmed in Kampala. Suspected Kinshasa case ruled out by INRB confirmatory testing. Africa CDC convenes high-level meeting including DRC, Uganda, South Sudan and donors.

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC — first ever without convening Emergency Committee first; second imported case confirmed in Kampala; as of this date: 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in DRC. (WHO PHEIC Notice)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC. Second imported Kampala case confirmed. WHO reports 8 lab-confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri. Kinshasa suspect tests negative on confirmatory INRB testing.

Second independent imported case confirmed in Kampala (no link to first case). WHO Director-General declares PHEIC — not pandemic emergency — under IHR Article 12. Africa CDC convenes high-level regional coordination meeting with 130+ participants.
WHO Director-General declares PHEIC (not pandemic emergency) for BDBV in DRC and Uganda. Second confirmed case reported in Kampala. Kinshasa suspect case tests negative (retracted).

WHO DG declares PHEIC for Ebola-BDBV in DRC and Uganda — 8th PHEIC under IHR (2005). As of this date: 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri; 2 confirmed imported cases in Kampala. Africa CDC convenes high-level consultative meeting with 130+ participants from affected and donor countries.
WHO Director-General declares Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

INRB/AFP confirms Goma case: wife of a Bunia Ebola fatality tested positive after traveling to Goma (North Kivu) while already infected, extending geographic spread beyond Ituri. (INRB via AFP / Al Jazeera)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Bundibugyo virus disease; CDC and US State Dept coordinate medical evacuation to Germany for treatment; 6 additional high-risk contacts also moved to Germany. (CDC / NBC News)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo; US officials coordinate evacuation of seven individuals to Germany for care. CDC confirms Level 2 travel health notice for DRC, Level 1 for Uganda.
WHO Emergency Committee to be convened; WHO Director-General confirms PHEIC declared without prior Emergency Committee recommendation — a first in WHO history, citing extraordinary urgency.
WHO formally announces PHEIC; does not declare pandemic emergency. INRB confirms first case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality. (WHO; INRB via AFP)
US missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia; CDC confirms an American has tested positive. (Serge charity; CDC briefing)

INRB Director Muyembe confirms laboratory-positive case in Goma, North Kivu (M23-held city of >1 million, on Rwandan border). Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. Rwanda closes Goma–Gisenyi border crossings indefinitely. American missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms first US national infected.

First confirmed case in Goma, North Kivu, reported — a woman who travelled from Ituri. Africa CDC raises figures to 336 suspected cases, 88 deaths, 13 confirmed. INRB director Muyembe confirms spread to North Kivu.

American physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms the first US national infected. Six other Americans classified as high-risk exposures; all to be moved to Germany for treatment and monitoring.

Confirmed case in Goma (North Kivu) announced by INRB Director Prof. Muyembe — wife of Bunia Ebola death who travelled to Goma while already infected. CDC confirms outbreak now affects at least 9 health zones in Ituri. US CDC triggers enhanced travel monitoring for DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

Confirmed case in Goma, North Kivu (wife of Bunia Ebola victim) reported by INRB director Prof. Muyembe to AFP; CDC transcript confirms 9 health zones affected in Ituri. (Al Jazeera / AFP / CDC Transcript)

American physician Dr. Peter Stafford (medical missionary, Serge organization) tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo disease in Ituri; CDC begins coordination for medical evacuation to Germany. (CDC Situation Summary)
Goma (North Kivu) case confirmed: wife of a Bunia Ebola death travelled to Goma while infectious. Outbreak now spans Ituri and North Kivu provinces.
American physician Dr. Peter Stafford (Serge/CTSM missionary at Nyankunde Hospital, Bunia) tests positive for BDBV — first confirmed American case in this outbreak.

First confirmed case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality who travelled while infected. Rwanda closes DRC border. CDC holds first public media briefing on outbreak; 9 health zones now affected in DRC.
US physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for BVD at Bunia hospital (confirmed 18 May); CDC and State Dept arrange medical evacuation of Stafford plus 6 high-risk contacts to Germany.
Confirmed BDBV case reported in Goma, Nord-Kivu. Outbreak now spans Ituri and Nord-Kivu. CDC issues Level 3 Travel Health Notice for DRC (reconsider nonessential travel), Level 1 for Uganda.
American surgeon Dr. Peter Stafford (Serge mission, Nyankunde Hospital, Bunia) tests positive for BDBV after unknowingly operating on an Ebola patient pre-outbreak confirmation.
Case confirmed in Goma, Nord-Kivu. Kinshasa suspected case retracted after INRB confirmatory test returned negative.
Outbreak expands from 3 to 9+ health zones in DRC. New confirmed case in Goma (under M23 rebel control). US CDC enacts enhanced travel screening.
Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); reports ~395 suspected cases and 106 associated deaths across DRC and Uganda. (Africa CDC)

CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening, Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who traveled to DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the prior 21 days; CDC EOC activated. (CDC / DHS)

CDC Situation Summary (most recent official update) reports 11 confirmed cases and 336 suspected cases including 88 deaths in DRC, and 2 confirmed cases including 1 death in Uganda across 9 health zones. (CDC Situation Summary)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths confirmed. US CDC/DHS invoke Title 42, restricting entry of non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in prior 21 days.

Ebola confirmed in Goma, North Kivu (rebel-held M23 city); Rwanda closes Goma-Gisenyi border crossings. Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. DRC Health Minister announces three new Ebola treatment centres opening in Ituri.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3(F) of Africa CDC Statute. 395 suspected cases, 106 associated deaths reported. (Africa CDC PHECS declaration)

CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 travel restrictions; entry restrictions placed on non-US passport holders from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan in previous 21 days. CDC moves 7 Americans (1 confirmed case + 6 high-risk contacts) to Germany for care. (CDC)
CDC current situation page confirms 9 health zones in Ituri Province now affected; EU announces PPE stockpiles ready for deployment and detection kit support to Africa CDC. (CDC; CNN)

Africa CDC formally declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 for at least 30 days restricting entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda or South Sudan within the previous 21 days. US moves 7 people (1 confirmed case, 6 high-risk contacts) from DRC to Germany for treatment/monitoring. US Embassy in Uganda temporarily suspends visa services. DRC Health Minister announces opening of 3 new Ebola treatment centres in affected region. WFP airlifts >5 tonnes of medical supplies to Ituri. OCHA reports 482 suspected cases and ~116 deaths in Ituri province alone.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3, Paragraph F of the Africa CDC Statute. CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening and Title 42 entry restrictions for travellers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan within 21 days. CDC confirms 9 health zones in Ituri affected. US State Department issues Do Not Travel advisory for DRC and South Sudan; Reconsider Travel for Uganda and Rwanda.

Africa CDC declares PHECS. American Christian missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford confirmed positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; US working to evacuate 7 Americans (1 positive, 6 high-risk) to Germany. CDC + DHS invoke Title 42 restricting entry of non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, South Sudan (21-day rule). Confirmed cases in Butembo (North Kivu) reported by WHO representative. DRC begins establishing field hospitals in Bunia. Total at CDC: 10 confirmed, 336 suspected, 88 deaths in DRC; 2 confirmed incl. 1 death Uganda.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3F; ~395 suspected cases and 106 deaths reported at time of declaration. US CDC and DHS implement Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda and South Sudan. (Africa CDC PHECS / CDC)
DRC authorities begin establishing field hospitals in Bunia after city hospitals overwhelmed; DRC health minister announces 3 Ebola treatment centres to be opened. (Wikipedia / PBS)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS invoke Title 42 entry restrictions: 30-day ban on non-US nationals who visited DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in preceding 21 days. CDC confirms 9 health zones affected in Ituri. CDC reports 10 confirmed, 336 suspected, 88 deaths (DRC) + 2 confirmed, 1 death (Uganda).

Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS invoke Title 42 — 30-day entry restriction for non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within prior 21 days. DRC opens field hospitals in Bunia after existing facilities overwhelmed.
Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS implement US Title 42 entry restrictions for non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

Cases identified in Butembo (Nord-Kivu) and Nyakunde (Ituri), bringing affected health zones to 11 (DRC) per CDC 20 May update. Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS invoke Title 42 entry restrictions: 30-day ban on non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the preceding 21 days.
American physician Peter Stafford confirmed positive for Bundibugyo virus disease on 17–18 May; first American case in the 2026 outbreak.

OCHA reports 482+ suspected cases since April in Ituri; confirms Goma case; warns hostile environment (insecurity, displacement, hunger) is severely hampering response; >5 tonnes of supplies airlifted to Ituri by WFP.
UN News and NBC report outbreak approaching ~500 suspected cases and 116 associated deaths; case in Beni (North Kivu) also reported; situation remains rapidly evolving.

OCHA and UN partners warn hostile environment in eastern DRC is severely hampering response; nearly 10 million people in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu face crisis-level hunger compounding outbreak risk. ECDC deploys expert to Africa CDC headquarters. Reuters witnesses Congolese nationals turned back at Bukavu-Rwanda border. Outbreak total now exceeds 482 suspected cases across at least 9 health zones per OCHA.

DRC daily health bulletin reports 516 suspected cases, 33 confirmed cases, and 131 deaths — including 26 new deaths in 24 hours. WHO representative Dr Anne Ancia confirms spread to North Kivu (Goma and Butembo). Butembo records first 2 confirmed cases (INRB). WHO technical advisory group convenes to assess vaccine options, including Ervebo (Merck) cross-protection potential; WHO notes 2-month timeline before any vaccine could be deployed.

CDC situation page updated: 536 suspected + 105 probable + 34 confirmed + 134 deaths across DRC and Uganda (2 confirmed + 1 death Uganda included). Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC and returned home develop symptoms; some transferred to Fort Portal for treatment. Uganda bans handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact. Germany confirms arrangements to receive American patient.

Confirmed cases reported in Butembo (North Kivu) by WHO field rep Dr. Ancia (UN News); Fort Portal, Uganda cases identified among Ugandans who attended DRC burial. CDC MoH figures: 536 suspected + 105 probable + 34 confirmed + 134 deaths. US State Dept issues Level 4 Do Not Travel for DRC, Uganda, South Sudan; commits $23M + funding for up to 50 treatment clinics. (CDC/State Dept/UN News)
Uganda government temporarily bans handshakes, hugs and unnecessary physical contact. (Wikipedia/AP)
Dr. Peter Stafford (American) safely evacuated from DRC to Germany for treatment; 6 high-risk American contacts also evacuated to Germany. (CDC / UPI / Serge)

Dr. Stafford airlifted to Charité Hospital, Berlin, Germany — first Ebola medical evacuation to Europe in this outbreak. Six high-risk US contacts evacuated to Germany and Czech Republic. Uganda bans handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact. DRC MoH reports ~500+ suspected, 131 deaths.

WHO DG Tedros expresses 'serious concern' over 'scale and speed' of epidemic at WHO Director-General briefing; DRC reports 513 suspected cases and 131 deaths. Dr. Stafford transported to Germany. Uganda bans handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact. UN News confirms cases in Butembo.

Chinese researchers publish multivalent mRNA vaccine study targeting EBOV, BDBV, and SUDV in PNAS; vaccine is pre-clinical (animal studies only). WHO vaccine official confirms two BDBV vaccine candidates under agency review.

Dr. Peter Stafford evacuated to Charité University Hospital, Berlin, Germany for treatment; wife Dr. Rebekah Stafford and 4 children evacuated to same hospital for monitoring. Dr. Patrick LaRochelle (potential exposure) sent to Bulovka Hospital, Prague.

WHO representative Dr. Anne Ancia confirms confirmed cases in both Butembo and Goma, Nord-Kivu; warns outbreak could take two months before a vaccine is available and recalls the 2018–2020 two-year response.

CDC confirms American physician Peter Stafford (missionary, Nyankunde Hospital) in transit to Berlin Charité hospital for treatment; 6 high-risk contacts moved to Germany and Czech Republic for monitoring.

WHO DG addresses World Health Assembly and media: 51 confirmed in DRC (Ituri and North Kivu), 2 confirmed in Uganda; ~600 suspected cases and 139 suspected deaths; Emergency Committee convened and agrees event is PHEIC but not pandemic emergency. (WHO DG Briefing 20 May 2026)

WHO reports ~600 suspected cases (51 confirmed) and 139 deaths in DRC + 2 confirmed (1 death) in Uganda. WHO DG warns of 'scale and speed' concern. Butembo cases confirmed in North Kivu. Ugandans who attended DRC burial taken to Fort Portal for treatment. Person in Ontario, Canada, tested for Ebola as precaution (result pending). White House reported to have resisted Dr. Stafford's return to US.

WHO Emergency Committee meets in Geneva; Tedros confirms ~600 suspected cases and 139 suspected deaths — largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever by factor >4x. Outbreak confirmed in 11 health zones across Ituri and Nord-Kivu. Ugandans who attended DRC burial develop symptoms; some taken to Fort Portal.

Person returning to Ontario, Canada from East Africa tested for Ebola as precautionary measure; result pending. US flights from DRC/Uganda/South Sudan redirected to Washington-Dulles for enhanced public health screening.
WHO Director-General Tedros confirms at press briefing: ~600 suspected cases, 139 suspected deaths, 51 confirmed in DRC, 2 imported in Uganda; PHEIC reaffirmed but not upgraded to pandemic emergency.
Group of Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC return to Uganda with Ebola symptoms; taken to Fort Portal for treatment and isolation.
Person who returned to Ontario, Canada from East Africa tested for Ebola as a precautionary measure; result reported as negative (no confirmed case).

WHO DG Tedros confirms to media: ~600 suspected cases, 139 suspected deaths; 51 confirmed cases in DRC (Ituri and Nord-Kivu); PHEIC status maintained; outbreak risk assessed as high nationally and regionally, low globally.

ECDC updates situation assessment (18:00 CET): confirms ~600 suspected cases and 139 deaths per WHO as of 20 May; Bahrain and other countries announce 30-day entry suspensions for travellers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan; Asian governments bolster border screening.

DHS orders all US-bound flights carrying passengers present in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within past 21 days to land at Washington-Dulles for enhanced health screening. Air France flight diverted to Montreal after DRC traveller boarded in error.

CDC/DRC-Uganda MoH report: 575 suspected cases, 51 confirmed, 148 deaths across 11 health zones. Dr. Stafford reports being 'cautiously optimistic' from Berlin hospital. White House denies Washington Post report of initial US refusal to allow repatriation.

First Ebola case confirmed in South Kivu Province by AFC/M23 rebel alliance (rural area near Bukavu); patient was a 28-yr-old man who travelled from Kisangani, Tshopo Province, hundreds of km from Ituri epicentre; UN separately confirms a second South Kivu case (woman contact of Beni travellers). Protests erupt in Rwampara over disputed Ebola death; police fire warning shots; two treatment tents burned.
All returning US citizens/residents from DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan required to enter the US exclusively via Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) for health screening.
India–African Union announce postponement of India-Africa Forum Summit (originally 28–31 May, New Delhi) citing 'emerging public health situation in Africa' — direct reference to Ebola outbreak.

Reuters/CNBC Africa reports WHO Africa regional director warns against underestimating Bundibugyo risk; DRC MoH May 21 bulletin: 670 suspected cases, 61 confirmed, 160 suspected deaths — highest figures to date.

alerts.title: Outbreak spreading to new DRC provinces — South Kivu confirmed 21 May
alerts.body: A confirmed Ebola case was reported 21 May in South Kivu Province (near Bukavu) — hundreds of kilometres from the Ituri epicentre — in a patient who travelled from Kisangani (Tshopo Province), where no cases had previously been reported. The UN separately confirmed a second South Kivu case. Geographic spread now encompasses Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu provinces of DRC.
alerts.source: AFC/M23 alliance via Reuters; UN Spokesman via multiple wire services; France 24

alerts.title: PHEIC declared — WHO 16 May 2026; Africa CDC PHECS 18 May 2026
alerts.body: WHO DG declared the BDBV outbreak in DRC and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 16 May 2026. Africa CDC declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May. No approved vaccine or therapeutic exists for Bundibugyo virus.

alerts.title: 670 suspected / 61 confirmed / 160 deaths — DRC MoH 21 May bulletin
alerts.body: DRC Health Minister Roger Kamba's 21 May figures: 670 suspected cases, 61 confirmed, 160 probable deaths — a rapid escalation from 246 suspected/80 deaths on 16 May. WHO DG warned on 20 May that case counts are expected to continue rising given the ~2-month undetected circulation period.
alerts.source: DRC Ministry of Health / Reuters / CNBC Africa

alerts.title: Fort Portal cluster — Ugandan burial attendees developing symptoms
alerts.body: A group of Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC around 18 May returned to Uganda and some developed Ebola-compatible symptoms; they have been taken to Fort Portal for treatment. This may represent the first secondary transmission chain outside Kampala within Uganda.
alerts.source: Wikipedia / Multiple sources citing Uganda MoH

alerts.title: No medical countermeasures available — containment relies on classic public health only
alerts.body: No licensed vaccine or specific therapeutic exists for Bundibugyo virus. Ervebo and monoclonal antibody products (Inmazeb, Ebanga) target Zaire ebolavirus epitopes only. CDC confirms it is exploring monoclonal antibody development. Response depends entirely on isolation, contact tracing, and safe burials in a high-insecurity environment.

alerts.title: US Title 42 entry restrictions and Dulles-only routing for returning Americans
alerts.body: On 18 May, CDC/DHS implemented Title 42 restrictions banning non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days. From 21 May, all US citizens/residents returning from those three countries must enter exclusively through Washington Dulles for health screening.

alerts.title: India-Africa Forum Summit postponed due to Ebola outbreak
alerts.body: India and the African Union announced on 21 May that the India-Africa Forum Summit (originally scheduled 28–31 May in New Delhi) has been postponed due to 'the emerging public health situation in Africa', in direct reference to the Ebola outbreak.
alerts.source: France 24 / India Ministry of External Affairs

news.title: WHO Africa chief: 'Big mistake' to underestimate Bundibugyo Ebola risk
news.summary: WHO Regional Director for Africa Mohamed Yakub warned on 22 May that even one case could spread Ebola beyond DRC and Uganda. The DRC MoH's 21 May bulletin reported 670 suspected cases, 61 confirmed, and 160 suspected deaths.

news.title: Ebola confirmed in DRC's South Kivu — hundreds of km from Ituri epicentre
news.summary: AFC/M23 rebel alliance confirmed a case near Bukavu on 21 May in a patient who had travelled from Kisangani, Tshopo Province. The UN separately confirmed a second South Kivu case — a woman contact of two individuals from Beni — whose 17-month-old child also died.

news.title: India-Africa Forum Summit postponed as Ebola outbreak escalates
news.summary: India and the African Union announced the postponement of the 28–31 May India-Africa Forum Summit in New Delhi, citing the 'emerging public health situation in Africa'. DRC officials have reported over 626 suspected cases and 159 suspected deaths as of 21 May.

news.title: Protests in Rwampara as Ebola death disputed; treatment tents burned
news.summary: On 21 May, residents in Rwampara, Ituri Province, protested after relatives disputed that Ebola had killed a young man and demanded his body. Police fired warning shots and tear gas; protesters set two treatment tents operated by a medical charity on fire.

news.title: WHO: ~600 suspected cases, 139 deaths; PHEIC status maintained as of 20 May
news.summary: WHO DG Tedros confirmed at a 20 May Geneva briefing that approximately 600 suspected cases and 139 suspected deaths have been reported, with 51 confirmed cases in Ituri and Nord-Kivu. WHO assessed national and regional risk as high, global risk as low.

news.title: American missionary Peter Stafford airlifted to Berlin Charité for Ebola treatment
news.summary: Peter Stafford, a US physician working at Nyankunde Hospital in Ituri, was confirmed BDBV-positive on 17–18 May and transported to Berlin's Charité hospital on 19 May — the first Ebola medical evacuation to Europe in this outbreak. Six high-risk contacts were moved to Germany and the Czech Republic.

news.title: Africa CDC declares continental Ebola emergency; convenes 130-country coordination meeting
news.summary: Africa CDC declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 18 May 2026 and convened a high-level meeting of 130+ participants from affected and at-risk countries, donors, and UN agencies on 16 May to align response priorities.

news.title: CDC/DHS invoke Title 42; US restricts entry from DRC, Uganda, South Sudan
news.summary: On 18 May, CDC and DHS implemented Title 42 restrictions banning entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days. From 21 May, all returning US citizens must enter via Washington Dulles International Airport for health screening.

news.title: ECDC deploys EU Health Task Force expert to Africa CDC HQ; assesses EU/EEA risk as very low
news.summary: ECDC is deploying an expert from the EU Health Task Force to Africa CDC headquarters and is liaising with WHO and EU Commission. The ECDC and EU assess the risk of infection for EU/EEA residents as very low given low probability of importation and secondary transmission in Europe.

news.title: WHO PHEIC declared — Ebola Bundibugyo in DRC and Uganda, 16 May 2026
news.summary: WHO DG declared the 8th PHEIC under IHR (2005) on 16 May, citing the outbreak's extraordinary nature: no approved countermeasures, high geographic spread risk, and a potentially much larger undetected outbreak. The declaration does not meet criteria for a pandemic emergency.

news.title: No vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo: CDC explores monoclonal antibody options
news.summary: With no licensed vaccine or therapeutic for BDBV, CDC is working with HHS agencies to develop a monoclonal antibody candidate; existing products Ervebo, Inmazeb, and Ebanga all target Zaire ebolavirus epitopes and are not expected to cross-protect. A Chinese mRNA candidate targeting three strains including BDBV remains in pre-clinical stages.

news.title: Bunia hospitals overwhelmed; field hospitals established as cases surge in Ituri
news.summary: As of 18 May, DRC health authorities began establishing field hospitals in Bunia, Ituri's capital, after existing hospitals became overwhelmed. CDC as of 20 May confirmed 11 health zones affected in Ituri and Nord-Kivu, with ongoing contact tracing severely hampered by insecurity.

background.virus: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV); formal species name Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus by ~30% genetic divergence — the same divergence that caused false-negative Xpert tests in 2026, delaying detection by ~10 days
background.case_fatality_rate_historical: 25–50% (WHO DON602: 30–50%; CDC: 25–50%; NBC News/Johns Hopkins expert: ~25–40%; previous outbreaks: 25% in 2007–08 Uganda, ~50% in 2012 DRC)
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces, fomites, or bodies of deceased individuals. Individuals are infectious only when symptomatic. Funeral/burial practices are a key transmission amplifier — demonstrated by the 2026 super-spreader event in Mongbwalu and the Fort Portal cluster from a DRC burial. Fruit bats are the suspected zoonotic reservoir.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding; nosebleeds and vomiting blood reported in current outbreak. Most current DRC cases are aged 20–39 and two-thirds are female (CDC). Co-infection with malaria is possible and should be considered.
background.vaccines_therapeutics: No approved vaccine/therapeutic for BDBV; Ervebo/Inmazeb/Ebanga target Zaire only; CDC developing monoclonal antibody candidate (May 2026); Chinese mRNA multi-strain candidate pre-clinical

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak; led to discovery and naming of the Bundibugyo strain; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel Orthoebolavirus species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus.
Second documented Bundibugyo outbreak; contained within months in a remote area; final BDBV outbreak prior to 2026.

Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, different species (Zaire ebolavirus), same geographic zone; Butembo was epicentre, now re-affected in 2026; response took over two years and is directly relevant precedent for current containment difficulties.

past_outbreaks.location: Bulape/Mweka Health Zones, Kasai Province, DRC (Ebola-Zaire)
past_outbreaks.notes: DRC's 16th Ebola outbreak, declared 4 September 2025; last patient discharged 19 October 2025; outbreak declared over December 2025; immediately preceded the current 2026 BDBV outbreak — DRC's second Ebola outbreak within 6 months.

past_outbreaks.location: Ituri Province (Mongbwalu, Rwampara, Bunia, Nyakunde + 7+ more HZs), Nord-Kivu (Goma, Butembo), Sud-Kivu (Bukavu rural) — DRC; Kampala, Fort Portal — Uganda
past_outbreaks.cfr: crude CFR undetermined due to large suspected-case denominator, ongoing diagnostic lag, and conflict-impeded surveillance
past_outbreaks.notes: Third and largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded by factor >4x; PHEIC declared by WHO 16 May 2026, PHECS declared by Africa CDC 18 May 2026; at least 12 health zones across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu; 2 confirmed imported cases in Kampala plus Fort Portal cluster (burial attendees); first American case evacuated to Berlin 19 May; South Kivu case confirmed 21 May — spread to 3rd DRC province.

why_this_matters: As of 22 May 2026, the DRC Health Minister reported 670 suspected cases, 61 confirmed, and 160 suspected deaths — already the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded by a factor of more than 4x the previous largest (149 cases in 2007–08), with cases escalating across at least 12 health zones and now spreading to a third DRC province (Sud-Kivu), hundreds of kilometres from the Ituri epicentre.

No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus; the two licensed Ebola vaccines (Ervebo/rVSV-ZEBOV; Zabdeno+Mvabea/Ad26.ZEBOV+MVA-BN-Filo) and licensed monoclonal antibodies (Inmazeb, Ebanga) target Zaire ebolavirus only; cross-protection against BDBV is not clinically established; CDC is exploring monoclonal antibody development; a Chinese mRNA multi-strain candidate is in pre-clinical stages only.

The outbreak has now expanded to three DRC provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu): Goma (pop. >1 million, Rwandan border, M23-controlled, airport closed) and Bukavu (South Kivu, also under M23/AFC control) represent the highest-risk nodes for regional and international spread due to rebel control preventing coordinated public health response.

A ~10-day diagnostic delay caused by false-negative standard Ebola Xpert assays (which target Zaire ebolavirus and cannot detect BDBV due to ~30% genomic divergence) allowed the outbreak to accumulate hundreds of cases before confirmation. Combined with an estimated 2-month undetected circulation before WHO was alerted, the true outbreak burden almost certainly significantly exceeds reported figures.

Active armed conflict across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu severely impedes response: M23/AFC controls Goma, Butembo, and Bukavu and operates a parallel health administration with no prior Ebola experience; ongoing militant attacks on health workers, community protests and tent-burning in Rwampara, and weak contact follow-up due to insecurity all undermine containment.

The confirmation of cases in South Kivu (21 May) via a patient who appears to have transited through Kisangani (Tshopo Province, a major DRC transport hub) — where no cases were previously recorded — signals an unknown onward transmission chain potentially operating outside the known geographic footprint of the outbreak.

International spread risk is real and escalating: Fort Portal, Uganda (burial cluster, 18 May); an American patient evacuated to Berlin (19 May); US Title 42 restrictions on DRC/Uganda/South Sudan; Dulles-only routing for returning Americans (21 May); India-Africa Forum Summit postponed (21 May); Hong Kong activating Ebola preparedness — all reflecting the widening international public health response.

With no medical countermeasures available and response depending entirely on classic outbreak containment — contact tracing, isolation, safe burials, community engagement — in one of the world's most complex and insecure operating environments, and with WHO warning that case counts are expected to continue rising given the long undetected circulation period, this is among the most challenging Ebola response scenarios since the 2018–2020 North Kivu outbreak.
